Original claim: The 14.22 standard-update SHA-256 is b0d5818d…706a810b.
Verification method: Stream the complete existing outer PUP through an independently authored SHA-256 verifier.
Observed result: Exact full digest match.
Limitations: File identity is not a Sony signature verification or retail-code analysis.
Final verdict: PASS: exact identity corroborated.

Original claim: The 14.22 outer package is 1,266,091,008 bytes.
Verification method: Read filesystem size and compare it with the documented value.
Observed result: Exact size match.
Limitations: No earlier firmware package was obtained.
Final verdict: PASS for this local package.

Original claim: The outer package is SLB2 version 3, flags 0x10000, with one entry.
Verification method: Independently unpack fixed-width little-endian fields and validate table extent.
Limitations: Container fields do not identify decrypted firmware components.
Final verdict: PASS for the observed header.

Original claim: PS5UPDATE1.PUP begins at sector 2, offset 1024.
Verification method: Decode the entry record, validate its name and in-file extent.
Observed result: Name, start and end 1,266,090,621 match.
Limitations: The entry is a protected PUP fragment, not an extracted ELF.
Final verdict: PASS: entry boundary corroborated.

Original claim: The first inner fragment is 1,266,089,597 bytes with SHA-256 7056fe13…7f668b1.
Verification method: Hash the existing inner file and independently hash exactly its declared range in the outer package.
Observed result: Both complete hashes and sizes match.
Limitations: Only the standard-update first fragment was checked, not recovery.
Final verdict: PASS: extraction identity corroborated.

Original claim: The 14.22 outer package ends with 387 zero padding bytes.
Verification method: Read all bytes after the declared entry end.
Observed result: 387 trailing bytes, all zero.
Limitations: Does not establish semantics of other reserved header areas.
Final verdict: PASS: padding verified.

Original claim: SLB2 block_count multiplied by 512 equals the file size.
Verification method: Check sector count, entry start alignment and outer size remainder.
Observed result: 2,472,834 sectors; exact total; zero outer remainder.
Limitations: The inner fragment length itself need not be sector aligned.
Final verdict: PASS: arithmetic and alignment verified.

Original claim: The 14.22 fragment has the documented 16-byte prefix and size fields 1456 / 3552.
Verification method: Read only the fixed prologue and preserve both byte-wise and integer interpretations.
Observed result: Prefix and raw values match.
Limitations: Other versions were not checked; version 272 versus byte value 16 reflects different field grouping, not the firmware number.
Final verdict: PASS for raw bytes; semantic field names remain qualified.

Original claim: The 14.22 SLB2 digest-like slot at 0x200 has the documented bytes.
Verification method: Read the slot without interpreting it as a verified checksum or key.
Observed result: Exact 32-byte value matches.
Limitations: The cryptographic function, keying and coverage remain unidentified.
Final verdict: PASS for bytes only.

Original claim: The encrypted inner fragment may have 44 segments by a header-size formula.
Verification method: Review arithmetic and check whether a readable segment table is available.
Observed result: The formula fits; the table is not readable.
Limitations: A size fit does not uniquely determine the format or actual count.
Final verdict: Retain as a hypothesis, never a decoded segment count.

Original claim: The inner update fragment is identified as a SELF-PROSPERO executable.
Verification method: Compare PUP context and GhidraProspero SELF detection conditions.
Observed result: The magic is shared; the loader additionally requires a structurally positioned inner ELF signature.
Limitations: The protected PUP does not expose an ELF header or executable structure here.
Final verdict: Use protected inner PUP or shared container family; executable identity is not established.

Original claim: Matching visible fields establish that recovery and standard fragments use the same protection scheme.
Verification method: Review the inference and the unavailable encrypted fields.
Observed result: Similar prefixes are reported, but keys, algorithms and protected metadata were not compared.
Limitations: No local recovery package and no decryption; shared visible fields are insufficient.
Final verdict: Weaken to reported visible-field similarity; identical cryptographic protection is not proven.

Original claim: Failed cryptographic attempts prove that PC decryption is impossible.
Verification method: Audit whether finite negative experiments establish the universal conclusion.
Observed result: The repository reports failed candidates, not an impossibility proof.
Limitations: No key search or decryption attempt was repeated in Phase 20.
Final verdict: State that decryption is unavailable in this workflow; remove proof-of-impossibility language.

Original claim: Recovery contains a byte-identical standard fragment plus a second protected fragment.
Verification method: Check availability of the claimed recovery input and raw comparison logs.
Observed result: Recovery input and comparison outputs are absent.
Limitations: Current local files contain only the standard update and its extracted first fragment.
Final verdict: Blocked pending the recovery package and original comparison evidence.

Original claim: The 14.22 outer package is 4096 bytes larger than 14.20.
Verification method: Check the two required package inputs.
Observed result: Only the 14.22 side is locally available.
Limitations: Arithmetic on two author-reported sizes is not an independent two-file comparison.
Final verdict: Keep the cross-version delta author-reported until both inputs are checked.

Original claim: The 117/115 differing-byte metric describes the compared header window.
Verification method: Read the detailed scope against the abbreviated summary.
Observed result: Detailed text limits the comparison to 0x000–0x440; summary wording can imply a whole-package difference.
Limitations: Earlier packages and raw comparison output are absent.
Final verdict: Always include the comparison window; never call this a firmware-code delta.

Original claim: All 677 compared syscall records matched an independent 13.60 reference.
Verification method: Trace input paths, claimed version and comparator provenance.
Observed result: The claim concerns 13.60; both original dump/reference data and raw comparison output are absent.
Limitations: A 13.60 comparison cannot validate 14.22 retail behavior.
Final verdict: Not independently reproduced; retain explicit 13.60 attribution.

Original claim: The older kernel dump contains 735 native syscall entries.
Verification method: Trace the referenced dump and parsed table.
Observed result: Neither input is shipped in the checkout.
Limitations: No kernel dump was downloaded or analysed in this phase.
Final verdict: Retain as an older-build reported result.

Original claim: Validation against 13.60 makes SDK-derived 14.22 addresses trustworthy.
Verification method: Examine the version-to-version inference and input availability.
Observed result: Checking an older build does not validate a newer retail image.
Limitations: No plaintext 14.22 executable or corresponding runtime observation is available.
Final verdict: SDK/source offsets are hypotheses about 14.22, not verified retail addresses.

Original claim: Mock chain completion demonstrates the software integration stages.
Verification method: Read CLI/test entry points and identify mocked memory/syscall responses; do not execute the chain.
Observed result: The documented success is a simulated integration result.
Limitations: No exploit implementation or kernel trigger was executed.
Final verdict: Accept only as a mock-software claim; it proves no retail jailbreak.

Original claim: The full chain operates end-to-end over a TCP primitive.
Verification method: Inspect the subprocess arguments of the demonstration.
Observed result: The TCP server is explicitly launched in mock-kernel mode.
Limitations: A real socket transport does not make the backing kernel real.
Final verdict: Describe it as TCP integration with a synthetic backend.

Original claim: Third-party beacon logs establish a working 14.22 browser memory primitive.
Verification method: Trace the claim to its attributed external observations and missing original capture/provenance.
Observed result: No authenticated, controlled 14.22 hardware observation is included locally.
Limitations: Borrowed probe labels and text logs do not independently establish native memory corruption or firmware identity.
Final verdict: Do not promote the hardware claim to independently verified.

Original claim: The first fixed retail hypervisor build is conclusively 14.10.
Verification method: Review the claimed inference and the document's admitted primary-source gaps.
Observed result: The document admits unavailable direct attribution and no patch date in the write-up.
Limitations: Not a controlled vulnerable/fixed retail build comparison.
Final verdict: Retain as reported attribution, not a verified first-fixed-build boundary.

Original claim: Public PlayStation source defaults prove JIT is off in retail firmware 14.22.
Verification method: Check pinned upstream build defaults and distinguish them from deployed configuration.
Observed result: Upstream ENABLE_JIT/FTL/DFG defaults are OFF; no retail build configuration is available.
Limitations: A public build default does not prove how Sony built or shipped 14.22.
Final verdict: Confirm the source default only; retail inference remains unverified.

Original claim: The PlayStation User-Agent token is not an exact engine revision identifier.
Verification method: Read the pinned upstream UserAgentPlayStation implementation.
Observed result: The token is a source literal; it is not a source revision digest.
Limitations: Current upstream source is not a mapped 14.22 executable.
Final verdict: Supported caution: do not infer exact deployed revision from the UA string.

Original claim: The cited NVD entries describe Apple-product issues and do not establish PS5 applicability.
Verification method: Fetch both current NVD API records independently and inspect descriptions/platform entries.
Observed result: Apple products are listed; no PS5 applicability or exact getContext mapping is stated in the checked records.
Limitations: Absence of PS5 in NVD is not proof that related shared code is unaffected.
Final verdict: PASS for the bounded NVD-content claim, not a PS5 patch conclusion.

Original claim: The particular canvas reentrancy issue is conclusively the cited CVE on PS5.
Verification method: Compare the asserted mapping with the authoritative advisory records.
Observed result: The examined NVD records do not establish that exact component/retail mapping.
Limitations: No matched advisory patch, deployed binary or controlled retail reproducer.
Final verdict: Treat the CVE-to-PS5 mapping as an external attribution.

Original claim: A valid freestanding ET_EXEC file is sufficient to establish console payload execution.
Verification method: Read the Makefile and inspect ELF headers without executing them.
Observed result: Ten tracked ELF copies represent five identical trigger pairs; they are ABI 0 / ET_EXEC.
Limitations: File format validity does not establish console ABI, syscall compatibility or execution.
Final verdict: Confirm header facts only; no retail compatibility or exploitation success was tested.

Original claim: The elfldr data_load helper copies p_filesz without explicit BSS-tail clearing.
Verification method: Compare the referenced helper with saved upstream v0.28 source and earlier decompilation.
Observed result: The helper copies file bytes; the analysed homebrew startup separately clears its BSS.
Limitations: This is a loader/runtime detail, not a firmware 14.22 finding; no console execution.
Final verdict: Use the narrow helper-level description and account for runtime initialization.

Original claim: The emulator executed 23,742 instructions from a genuine game executable.
Verification method: Trace the stated input and full execution log.
Observed result: The game executable and run log are absent from the local repository.
Limitations: No proprietary game image was acquired; source contains service shims, not a full console environment.
Final verdict: Not independently reproduced and not firmware 14.22 execution.

Original claim: The chance of a 14.22 jailbreak without console access is 5–10 percent.
Verification method: Look for a defined population, model, calibration and measured outcome data.
Observed result: No defensible quantitative probability model is supplied.
Limitations: This is not a statistically estimable probability from the available evidence.
Final verdict: Retain UNKNOWN in the official project status.

Original claim: The runner's ALL PASS summary means every intended check was performed.
Verification method: Read missing-dependency branches and their calls to step_end.
Observed result: Some skipped checks are explicitly recorded as PASS.
Limitations: The suite was not executed; this is a source-level accounting finding.
Final verdict: Report PASS/SKIP separately; a green summary is not complete test coverage.

Original claim: The documented stage and test totals describe one consistent current run.
Verification method: Compare README, report, runner and expected-stage source at the same commit.
Observed result: 12/13 stages, 7/9 steps and 17/19 tests coexist without one pinned raw run manifest.
Limitations: These can be stale documentation rather than failed execution; exact current totals were not rerun.
Final verdict: Record metric drift; do not choose whichever historical count looks best.

Original claim: Repository A is offered under an MIT licence.
Verification method: Inspect the tracked licence file and inventory.
Observed result: MIT grant is present.
Limitations: The grant does not transfer rights in excluded third-party proprietary firmware.
Final verdict: PASS for the repository's original licensed material.

Original claim: The author's research workspace contains 32,349 files and 5.4 GB.
Verification method: Compare the statement's private-workspace scope with the incorporated checkout.
Observed result: The checkout has 220 tracked files and 2,925,085 bytes; the larger workspace is not supplied.
Limitations: A private-workspace size is not necessarily a claim about the published checkout.
Final verdict: Do not reproduce the private-workspace metric as this checkout's inventory.

Original claim: The repository does not ship Sony firmware binaries.
Verification method: Inventory tracked file types, sizes and ELF duplicates.
Observed result: No PUP input or kernel dump is present; ten small trigger ELF copies are present.
Limitations: Filename/type inventory alone cannot attest provenance of every embedded byte.
Final verdict: Publish no binaries or third-party code; retain the bounded inventory finding.

Original claim: The documented firmware comparisons are reproducible from named input/output artefacts.
Verification method: Check explicit repository-relative input and output paths.
Observed result: Eight of nine selected required paths are absent; the self_probe source itself is present.
Limitations: Only selected explicit references were tested; absence from this checkout is not proof the author never had them.
Final verdict: PARTIAL reproducibility: request the original permissible evidence rather than inventing it.

Original claim: Non-shared integer typed-array Atomics operations must throw TypeError.
Verification method: Compare the current ECMAScript algorithms with a bounded desktop control and the original reviewed diagnostic.
Observed result: All nine tested ordinary load/store/RMW operations succeed; the original diagnostic marks all nine unexpected.
Limitations: Chromium is a standards control, not PS5 firmware reproduction.
Final verdict: Correct the expected outcomes; these successes are not a vulnerability signal.

Original claim: The suite targets and reflects firmware 14.22 on a Slim disc console.
Verification method: Review provenance and presence of raw per-run hardware observations.
Observed result: No recorded device/firmware attestation or reproducible console run is shipped.
Limitations: The pages can run on other browsers and print the same target label.
Final verdict: Target label is metadata, not verified firmware attribution.

Original claim: The slow chain stops at a total of 320 MB and avoids the allocation ceiling.
Verification method: Statically sum all retained warm-up, ramp and retry buffers without allocating them.
Observed result: 15 + 880 + 10 = 905 MiB retained if all allocations succeed.
Limitations: 905 MiB is requested backing-store extent, not measured resident memory.
Final verdict: Replace the total-cap/safety claim and account for cumulative retention.

Original claim: The pressure page performs forty allocation steps while retaining prior buffers.
Verification method: Review the loop and multiply step size by its maximum iterations.
Observed result: The 256 MiB option can request 10,240 MiB; 64/128 options request 2,560/5,120 MiB.
Limitations: No pressure loop was executed and no physical-memory ceiling was measured.
Final verdict: Classify as a high-memory stress page, not a low-impact capability check.

Original claim: Touching only the first and last byte establishes committed memory for the whole allocation.
Verification method: Inspect the writes and distinguish logical buffer extent from resident-page accounting.
Observed result: Only two endpoint locations are explicitly written; no resident-memory measurement is made.
Limitations: No operating-system memory commitment experiment was performed.
Final verdict: Do not report allocated extent as measured resident or fully touched memory.

Original claim: The first failed allocation measures the firmware-wide memory ceiling.
Verification method: Review the tested size sequence, failure handling and missing process-state controls.
Observed result: The result depends on process state, resource pressure and implementation; the next finer boundary is not searched.
Limitations: Large-allocation mode was intentionally not executed.
Final verdict: Report only the largest tested size under a recorded run context.

Original claim: An opaque sandbox frame returning null contentDocument is a failing diagnostic result.
Verification method: Run the reviewed iframe page and an independent small opaque-origin control.
Observed result: Normal isolation produces null and is displayed with the page's fail class.
Limitations: A normal desktop boundary check does not test PS5 sandbox escape.
Final verdict: Label expected isolation separately from failure.

Original claim: The iframe page meaningfully tests postMessage for both ordinary and sandboxed frames.
Verification method: Trace the early return and verify the original page's observed paths.
Observed result: The sandbox-null branch returns before postMessage; there is no child echo acknowledgement.
Limitations: A send without a receiver is not an end-to-end messaging test.
Final verdict: Add an explicit reply protocol in a benign future diagnostic; the present sandbox message test is absent.

Original claim: Overlapping typed-array views expose writes through the shared buffer.
Verification method: Run only the reviewed small views test and compare with an independent 4-byte DataView control.
Observed result: The observed 32-bit value matches the little-endian control.
Limitations: Byte order is implementation-relevant; this is ordinary view behavior, not arbitrary process memory access.
Final verdict: PASS for desktop semantics only.

Original claim: Transferring an ordinary ArrayBuffer detaches the sender.
Verification method: Run the reviewed views-only test plus a 512-byte MessageChannel receive/verify control.
Observed result: Sender length becomes zero; receiver retains 512 bytes and marker value 42.
Limitations: Feature availability varies; no PS5 result is inferred.
Final verdict: PASS for the bounded desktop transfer check.

Original claim: The minimal Wasm page can compile, instantiate and grow memory from one to eleven pages.
Verification method: Run this fully reviewed small page on isolated desktop Chromium.
Observed result: Compile and instantiate succeed; grow returns one and final size is eleven 64 KiB pages.
Limitations: This is desktop capability, not a PS5 Wasm/JIT observation.
Final verdict: PASS for the desktop diagnostic only.

Original claim: The sniff page checks secure context, isolation and SharedArrayBuffer exposure independently.
Verification method: Use a loopback control with and without COOP/COEP headers.
Observed result: Both contexts are secure; only the isolated one exposes SharedArrayBuffer in the observed browser.
Limitations: Header and embedding policy matter; missing SAB does not prevent ordinary non-shared Atomics operations.
Final verdict: Record origin, headers and context, not merely a target firmware label.

Original claim: A green final chain status reflects success of all preceding stages.
Verification method: Read the catch paths and the unconditional final status paint; do not run the chain.
Observed result: Some errors are caught and execution continues to an unconditional green final status.
Limitations: No pressure or chain routine was executed.
Final verdict: A final green square is not a conjunction of stage results.

Original claim: The README's Quick Scan/menu inventory describes the current interface.
Verification method: Compare the tracked README page list with current index.html and the file inventory.
Observed result: Current index has no Quick Scan function; three newer pages are omitted from the README list.
Limitations: Documentation drift is not evidence of browser engine behavior.
Final verdict: Update the page inventory and remove stale UI descriptions.

Original claim: A restart during these probes can be identified as a kernel panic by the page.
Verification method: Review the available observation and logging channels.
Observed result: The HTML has no kernel crash telemetry or panic attribution mechanism.
Limitations: A video of a restart alone cannot distinguish OOM, browser failure and kernel panic.
Final verdict: Use observed symptom language unless independent crash evidence exists.

Original claim: Missing feature flags are displayed as failures in the sniff page.
Verification method: Read the feature-label mapping and distinguish optional API availability from conformance.
Observed result: Every absent listed API receives fail styling, including implementation/context-dependent APIs.
Limitations: This styling does not establish a security vulnerability or standards failure.
Final verdict: Use available/unavailable/context-restricted labels.

Original claim: Repository B is publicly available diagnostic material.
Verification method: Inspect all tracked files for an explicit licence grant.
Observed result: Eleven tracked files contain no LICENSE file or explicit licence grant in README.
Limitations: Public visibility does not supply a redistribution licence.
Final verdict: Link to source; do not republish its HTML/JavaScript in the audit bundle.
